title: Regular and irregular verbs
metaTitle: Irregular verbs list: past simple and past participle – Reference – EnglishAcademy
description: Regular and irregular English verbs at a glance: the -ed spelling rules, then the irregular verbs grouped by pattern, with he/she/it, past simple and past participle.
lead: A verb is regular (past with -ed) or irregular. The irregular verbs are grouped by pattern: verbs that change in the same way are easier to learn together.

sections.name: Regular verbs
sections.what: The past simple and the past participle end in -ed and are the same. Most verbs are regular, and new verbs are too: google, googled.
regel: Pattern: *work – worked – worked.* The past simple and the past participle are the same.
The verb ends in -e: add only -d: *live – lived, decide – decided.*
Consonant + y: y becomes -ied: *study – studied, carry – carried.* But vowel + y stays: *play – played.*
One short stressed vowel + one consonant: double the consonant: *stop – stopped, plan – planned, prefer – preferred.* British English also doubles l: *travel – travelled* (US: *traveled*).
Say -ed as an extra syllable /ɪd/ only after t and d: *wanted, decided.* After other sounds it is /t/ or /d/: *worked, played.*

sections.name: Irregular verbs: past simple ≠ past participle
sections.what: The past simple and the past participle are different words. Learn all three forms together.
regel: Pattern: *write – wrote – written.* The past simple stands alone: *I wrote.* The participle comes after have/has/had and in the passive: *I have written, it was written.*
Don't use the participle as a past simple: *I saw it* (not *I seen it*), *she went* (not *she gone*).
Verbs with the same vowel change are easiest to learn together: *sing – sang – sung, drink – drank – drunk.*
*be* has two past forms: *I/he/she/it was, you/we/they were*; the participle is *been.*
items: # i – a – u: sing, sang, sung
# i – o – i…en: write, wrote, written
# Base form = past participle: come, came, come
I was, you were, he was, we were, they were.
He has gone to work (he is there now). He has been to Paris (and come back).

sections.name: Irregular verbs: past simple = past participle
sections.what: The past simple and the past participle are the same irregular form, so there are only two forms to learn.
regel: Pattern: *buy – bought – bought.* One form for *I bought* and *I have bought.*
Many end in -ought or -aught: *buy, bring, think, fight → bought, brought, thought, fought; catch, teach → caught, taught.*
Some don't change at all: *cut – cut – cut, put – put – put.* Only he/she/it in the present adds -s: *she puts.*
British English: *get – got – got.* US English often has *have gotten.*
items: # Long vowel → short vowel: sleep, slept
says and said rhyme with bed: /sez/, /sed/.
Same spelling, different sound: read /riːd/, past read /red/.
